title: Lettre Tate (mai 66) (Cristaux) : lettre (1966), tapuscrit (s.d.), notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: Grothendieck is setting up a theory of crystals with Frobenius over a base S of characteristic p, in the 1966 letter to Tate and the related typescript. On the previous page he introduces three things. First, p-crystals (M, F: M^(p) → M). Second, bicrystals of weight i, which also carry V: M → M^(p) with FV = VF = p^i. Third, crystals up to isogeny (isocrystals), and among them bi-isocrystals, meaning p-isocrystals with F an isomorphism, with no choice of weight.

The top of this page finishes that discussion. The bi-isocrystal notion contains all the 'bicrystal of weight i up to isogeny' categories, which embed fully faithfully and nest as i increases. It is also stable under tensor product and duality; the clause 'et passage au dual' is a handwritten addition. Grothendieck therefore proposes bi-isocrystals as the natural target category for a 'de Rham cohomology' functor once one works up to isogeny. In modern terms: rational crystalline cohomology takes values in F-isocrystals.

1.12, Example 1: S = Spec k with k perfect, and W = W(k).
- A crystal of finite-type modules on k is the same as a finite W-module M.
- Frobenius pullback is M^(p) = M ⊗_{W,σ} W, where σ = f_W is the Witt-vector Frobenius.
- A p-crystal structure is a σ-semilinear F: M → M.
- Since σ is an automorphism, x ↦ x⊗1 is a σ-semilinear bijection M → M^(p). Hence a 'p^{-1}-structure' M → M^(p) amounts to a σ^{-1}-semilinear V: M → M.
- (F, V) is a bicrystal of weight i iff FV = VF = p^i. For i = 1 these are exactly Dieudonné modules, so Dieudonné crystals over k are equivalent to Dieudonné modules.
- Isocrystals of finite type are equivalent to finite-dimensional vector spaces over K = Frac W.
- Hence a finite-type bi-isocrystal over k is a finite-dimensional K-space with a bijective σ_K-semilinear endomorphism. This is the modern F-isocrystal over k, the object later classified by the Dieudonné–Manin theorem.

The next page characterises the effective objects and the Tate twist, then passes to S smooth over k.
errors: V_M is called 'f_W^{-1}-linéaire'; it should read f_W^{-1}-semi-linéaire. The earlier sentence states this correctly, so it is only a slip.
Minor point: the identification of a crystal over Spec k with a W-module tacitly takes crystals relative to W (or Z_p) and p-adically complete; this is fine for modules of finite type.

ideas.what: Bi-isocrystals (F-isocrystals with F bijective, no weight fixed) as the right target for de Rham/crystalline cohomology up to isogeny, stable under tensor product and duality
ideas.modern_name: F-isocrystals; rational crystalline cohomology with values in F-isocrystals
ideas.where_published: Grothendieck, 'Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes' (Dix exposés, 1968); ICM Nice 1970 'Groupes de Barsotti-Tate et cristaux'; Montréal 1970 lectures

ideas.what: Bicrystals of weight i: F, V with FV = VF = p^i; weight 1 gives Dieudonné modules
ideas.modern_name: F-crystals with Verschiebung / 'F-V-modules of weight i' (cf. Mazur, Ogus, Fontaine)
ideas.where_published: Montréal 1970 lectures (Groupes de Barsotti-Tate et cristaux de Dieudonné) treat the Dieudonné case

ideas.what: Over a perfect field: crystal = W-module, M^(p) = M ⊗_σ W, p-structure = σ-semilinear F, p^{-1}-structure = σ^{-1}-semilinear V; isocrystal = K-vector space with bijective σ-semilinear map
ideas.modern_name: Dieudonné modules / F-isocrystals over a perfect field

deep.surprise_reason: This is a standard, foundational dictionary (Dieudonné modules, F-isocrystals over a perfect field) that Grothendieck himself published around 1968–70 and that became textbook material through Berthelot and Ogus. The weight-i bicrystal framing is a mild early variant, but not new.
transcription_corrections: 'V_M : M→M' is given in the image as f_W^{-1}-'linéaire' with letters overtyped; the transcription is correct, but the mathematics requires 'semi-linéaire'.
The handwritten insertion is 'et passage au dual.', placed after 'tensoriel'.
Strikeout before 'Exemple': the '1' is a handwritten insertion, i.e. 'Exemple 1'.
The handwritten 'K' replaces a struck-out symbol for the fraction field of W; f_K replaces a struck-out exponent.
